newsitem.title: UK: Pilkington lower in weak building sector.
newsitem.headline: Pilkington lower in weak building sector.

text.p: Pilkington Plc led the UK building materials sector lower on Tuesday amid fears of rising interest rates in the UK and worries that it may lose its membership of the FTSE 100 index, dealers and analysts said.
Pilkington shares fell 5p to 154p by 1128 GMT -- after touching a 19-month low of 153p -- with dealers saying the building material sector as a whole was attracting sellers.
Blue Circle Industries Plc lost 8p to 365-1/2p, RMC Group Plc dropped 6p to 996p and Redland Plc was down 7-1/2p to 395p.

"There is a bit of stock around in the sector and there are pre-budget fears of a base rate rise, which does sound a bit contrary to what the rest of the market is doing," said an analyst at one leading brokerage.
"The outlook in Germany is pretty bleak where Pilkington, Redland and RMC have exposure but the sector just seems to be having a sell-off ahead of the budget."

Dealers also pointed out that Pilkington could lose its membership of the FTSE 100 index after the FTSE committee meets next Wednesday to review memebership of the index and this has contributed to the shares weakness.
Also the recent strength of pound against the mark has the effect of shrinking the sterling value of the profits companies make in Germany.
